title: "GULLYPASS COLLECTION"
paragraph_01: For a while during the creation of my last deathrun map, I had in mind to create something based upon an area that I could see from driving home from the Cabin, that was a steep slope between two mountains where it went down for miles with forest ending only in a lake at the bottom and then going right back up another mountain
paragraph_02: The idea still lingers with me even now for a potential level for a game, but I knew that I had to try to make it come to vision
paragraph_03: This area that I had mind lies from a road goes from the Geilo to Tunhovd, down to Rødberg, that crosses the lake that is between this area. Having taken this road quite a few times, this place stuck on my head for a while
paragraph_04: This was around the time I came in contact with the greater TF2 community when I was introduced by the Artist that made the logos for my maps at that time
paragraph_05: Gullypass was that idea, and it was designed in a way where both teams would start on a road from each other between the two slopes, where they had to run down that slope to reach a cabin in the middle of the map, that would contain the objective being the control point
paragraph_06: The map is set in a said fjord somewhere in Norway where both the RED and BLU team attack a Radio Station broadcasting some messages that they intend to control. The map is surrounded with a huge valley that goes for miles along outside the maps boundaries.
paragraph_07: Gradually as I developed it went from first just being a simple HUT in the middle of the map, to being a radio station to give some proper meaning to attacking the map
paragraph_08: Gullypass released to mixed receptions, while it was praised for its visuals and the playtesters did enjoy it, the overall vision of the map did seem to resonate with players that much unfortunately due to some lighting factors and the map's overall design
paragraph_09: Not long after having developed Gullypass, I sat down to create the Halloween variant of the map, for the Halloween session update that same year
paragraph_10: Gullycreak would be made different, by that a portal would occasionally above the control point in the radio tower that had been ripped apart, that when entered would send you the map's underworld, where you'd need to traverse an obstacle course in order to escape the underworld. That and the new style of the map that would match the Halloween feeling
paragraph_11: This was also the map when I begun working with an Artist who would be creating the promotional material for the map, such as its logo and Steam frames. Thanks to them I was able to promote the map better, and we had a solid working relationship to when I stopped working on the Source Engine
